plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. This is because any bid below your value risks losing the auction to a slightly higher bid, even if it's below your value, resulting in zero profit. Bidding above your value risks winning but paying more than the item is worth to you. Since this is round 1 and there is no history, I will bid my true value.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy converges to bidding your true value. Any lower bid risks losing the auction to someone bidding slightly above your reservation price, while bidding higher than your value guarantees a loss. My value is $30. Therefore, I will bid my true value.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Since values are between $0 and $20, a reasonable expectation for the second-highest bid is around $10. However, my value is $30, so I can afford to bid higher. I will bid a value that is significantly higher than the expected second highest bid, but still below my value.
